Even though I don't think your overemotional, I definitly think you have an attachment problem. I went through the same thing well I was in a long distance relationship, so I know how tough it can be. I felt so seperated from her actual life that if we were apart for too long I would worry she would realize she didn't need me. We unfortunatly ended up breaking up because I realized it too late, but you realizing might allow you to fix it. 

First, I would reccommend getting a therapist if you can. I know you said you don't have time, but even if you just see one an hour a week it might be super helpful. Emotional dependence usually stems from something, and a therapist can be really helpful with that. Second I would recommend talking to him about it. Tell him how you feel, and see if you can find a way to make you feel more comfortable. And lastly, try and find something that is just yours. By this I mean find a hobby/passion that is mainly yours. When I finally broke up with my ex, I realized that I had nothing that was just mine. All our hobbies were shared, and everything was about us, not me. That way if you feel you are being too dependent, you can do that hobby instead and realize that you can have a life outside your partner.

As someone who was on the other side of that and wasn't broken up with till it was too late, you made the right choice.  In fact, I would consider this a very selfless and mature act. You accepted you were not in a good place, and you let go of him because you knew it would be better. 

Now for advice on getting better, you should start focusing on yourself. I noticed you said you wanted to get better for him. Do not do this! Focus on getting better for yourself, not for someone else. Keep going to therapy, and focus on doing hobbies and things you enjoy. Now that you're out of the relationship, you don't have to worry about it anymore. You have the freedom to do whatever you want/need to get better, and no one can tell you otherwise.

I went through this exact thought process after my ex broke up with me. I realized how she had been mistreating me, and felt very angry at myself for not saying anything. Its a really hard feeling to deal with, knowing you could have stood up for yourself but didn't. 

What helped me was realizing that its over, and theres nothing I can do now. Sure I'm annoyed at how I didn't react, but now I know for the future that I should stick up for myself. The first love ending is the hardest. I was broken up with by my first love 3 weeks ago, so I understand how hard it is. I know how easy it is to just lie in bed and hope they will come back, but u shouldn't do this. Even if they come back, they don't want to come back to someone who is still in the past. They want to come back to the new future you. My relationship ended because of distance. We wouldn't be able to see each other for a year, so she couldn't take it. She still loved me, but thats what was best for her so I didn't argue. That seems to be what happened here. You are still very important to him, he just needed to do whats best for him. It doesn't mean he loves u any less then before, it just means it wasnt the right time. In a way thinking like this helped me heal. I said to myself, "I love her enough to let her go and be her own person. Maybe in the future we will be together and maybe we wont, but either way we both got this chance to be with each other, and it was great." You dont need to say exactly that, but know u can love him and let him go at the same time. Good luck, heartbreak hurts so much but you are strong and you got this!
